Both unaligned segments hang off the one free hub n4580663526 (7,8), and its four neighbours 16(12,8), 3(7,13), 4(0,5), 7(8,1) are all ring members with four distinct columns and four distinct rows — so any single cell can close at most two of them, which is exactly what (7,8) already does (8-16 on row 8, 8-3 on column 7). The quadrant rule pins the hub to c<=8, r in [5,13]; inside that box the only other two-alignment cells are (0,8) and (8,13), and both are swallowed by a ring edge (4-13 on column 0, 0-3 on row 13), while (8,8)/(7,5)/(8,5) trade one alignment for another at hv 18. hv 18/20 and hvd 18 are therefore the ceiling, not a plateau. Round 1's edge trim (17x17 -> 14x16) already took every band outside the ring, and the three outside points are pinned by the quadrant rule (2 must sit on row 0 under 7; 5 and 9 must sit on rows 14 and 15 under 3; 10 must sit on column 13 east of 16). Nothing else in the layout can be tightened without losing an alignment.
